title: The Little Star That Loved to Shine

pages.text: High in the night sky lived a little star. She was very, very small. But she loved to shine.
sentences: High in the night sky lived a little star.
She was very, very small.
But she loved to shine.
pages.alt: A tiny glowing star with a smiling face high in a dark blue sky among bigger stars.

pages.text: Shine, shine, shine, went the little star. But the big stars were so bright, and nobody noticed her.
sentences: Shine, shine, shine, went the little star.
But the big stars were so bright, and nobody noticed her.
pages.alt: The little star glows beside much bigger, brighter stars.

pages.text: ‘I am too small,’ sighed the little star. ‘Nobody needs a tiny light like mine.’ And she felt a little sad.
sentences: ‘I am too small,’ sighed the little star.
‘Nobody needs a tiny light like mine.’ And she felt a little sad.
pages.alt: The little star looks down, her glow dimmer, looking sad.

pages.text: The Moon heard her sigh. ‘Little star,’ said the Moon, ‘keep shining. Every light has a job to do.’
sentences: The Moon heard her sigh.
‘Little star,’ said the Moon, ‘keep shining.
Every light has a job to do.’
pages.alt: A big kind moon speaks to the little star in the night sky.

pages.text: Far below, a traveller was walking home. The path was dark, and the big stars were hiding behind a cloud.
sentences: Far below, a traveller was walking home.
The path was dark, and the big stars were hiding behind a cloud.
pages.alt: A woman carrying a bundle walks along a dark path under a cloud-covered sky.

pages.text: ‘Oh dear,’ said the traveller. ‘I cannot see the path.’ Then she saw a tiny light peeping through a gap in the cloud.
sentences: ‘Oh dear,’ said the traveller.
‘I cannot see the path.’ Then she saw a tiny light peeping through a gap in the cloud.
pages.alt: The traveller looks up as one small star shines through a gap in the clouds.

pages.text: Shine, shine, shine, went the little star, as bright as she could. The traveller followed the tiny light, one step, two steps, three steps.
sentences: Shine, shine, shine, went the little star, as bright as she could.
The traveller followed the tiny light, one step, two steps, three steps.
pages.alt: The traveller follows a faint path of starlight along the ground.

pages.text: Soon the traveller was safe at home. ‘Thank you, little star,’ she whispered. The little star smiled. Now she knew that even a small light can help. Goodnight, little star. The end.
sentences: Soon the traveller was safe at home.
‘Thank you, little star,’ she whispered.
The little star smiled.
Now she knew that even a small light can help.
Goodnight, little star.
The end.
pages.alt: The traveller waves at the sky from her doorway as the little star twinkles above.

activities.question: How did the little star feel at first?
Who did the little star help?

activities.prompt: The path is dark and the big stars are hiding. What do you think will happen?
What happened first, next and last?
items: The little star felt too small.
The traveller could not see the path.
The star’s light showed her the way home.

activities.prompt: Have you ever felt small? What can you do that is special?

glossary.definition: A person who is going on a journey.
A white or grey shape in the sky made of tiny drops of water.
